title: Jumia Food's Last December, Thirteen Months After Its Founders Left
conflicts: Who decided: the slate named all four co-founders, but Kehinde and Afaedor had left years earlier (2014 per The Condia) and Poignonnec and Hodara stepped down in November 2022; the food exit was made by Francis Dufay's management under a board mandate, so the founder field names Dufay and records the co-founders' departure. Food's weight: about 11% of GMV in 9M 2023 (TechCrunch, TechCabal, Business Daily) vs 20% of items sold in Q3 2022 (TechCrunch); both given as different measures. No job-loss number was published for the food closure itself; the 900 (20%) figure is for the cuts from Q4 2022 and is reported as such.
notes: The 'several markets' of the slate are told as the seven-country food closure (Dec 2023) after earlier food exits from Egypt, Ghana and Senegal; the South Africa and Tunisia exits (2024) and the 2026 figures are aftermath, the latter attributed to an article on Jumia's own site. The edition is about a successor executive rather than a founder; the editor may want to confirm that suits the app.
